scores.evidence: Docs change often, citations need retrieval, and fine-tuning can't track edits (cited basis)
scores.rationale: Technical claims about RAG vs fine-tuning, eventual consistency of the index, citation validation, pgvector scale limits, and even sampling error at n=200 are all accurate and precisely stated.

scores.evidence: in v1 the bot only answers questions from public help-center articles and hands off to a human through your existing ticketing system
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities (accounts, restricted docs, languages) with explicit justified defaults and deferrals, and is clearly buildable by a small team.

scores.evidence: the help center is the system of record for content, and the bot never edits it… The ticketing system is the system of record for escalations
scores.rationale: Clear ownership of every component and data flow, and decisions made once (ingestion-time filtering, no model tools, index versioning) are honored consistently across phases with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: LLM-judge faithfulness calibrated against support-lead labels on 100 answers… Unsupported-claim rate ≤ 2% (ASSUMPTION)
scores.rationale: V0–V6 tie checkable thresholds to the specific worst failures, risky assumptions gate exposure, thresholds are honestly labeled provisional, and validation continues post-launch via SLOs, weekly review and quarterly red-teams.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: a conservative stopgap until the privacy owner sets the policy (before Phase 4)
scores.rationale: Every number carries an ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN/BASELINE label, missing inputs are listed with who supplies them, and the plan states exactly what changes if key assumptions are wrong ('Tell me if that applies and I'll re-plan').

scores.evidence: Worst failure: the bot confidently states a wrong or made-up policy… and the customer acts on it
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—hallucinated policy, restricted-content leak, injection, stale citations, runaway spend, abuse, feedback poisoning, LLM outage—each with concrete detection (diffs, planted articles, synthetic PII) and recovery.

scores.evidence: Rollback means redeploying the previous image digest, with the flag off as the kill switch
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback (including index blue/green and prompt pinning), domain-meaningful metrics, alerting, named owners, and an explicit complexity budget sized to one small team are in place from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: Cost per resolved conversation < human cost per ticket (UNKNOWN: support lead supplies it before Phase 4)
scores.rationale: Identifies inference as the dominant driver, imposes hard token/turn/spend caps with an automatic kill switch, grounds the build-vs-buy trade-off in per-resolution pricing, and measures rather than inventing figures.

scores.evidence: Corpus boundary… R3: showing internal articles to the public cannot be undone
scores.rationale: Explicit R2/R3 classification concentrates care on the irreversible choices (data to vendor, corpus boundary, answer scope) with validation gates, revisit triggers, and seams (ModelClient, pinned index versions) for the reversible ones.

scores.evidence: One service (API + ingestion worker), one managed Postgres with pgvector, one hosted LLM API; no self-hosted model or vector cluster
scores.rationale: Simplest workable stack with a stated complexity budget, reranker and routing added only if evals demand it, and nothing essential (eval, escalation, privacy, guardrails) sacrificed for that simplicity.

scores.evidence: Exit check: V1 and V2 pass. A synthetic runaway session is cut off at the cap and emits a cost metric
scores.rationale: A concrete day-zero slice, dependency-justified phase ordering, specific exit checks per phase, and explicit fallback actions when each validation fails let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: webhook-driven incremental sync, a nightly full reconcile, and unpublish handled as a priority delete
Chunk schema: article section with heading path, plus metadata (article ID, locale, product, updated_at, visibility)
Labeled eval set of at least 200 PII-scrubbed real questions with their source passages, plus at least 100 questions the docs don't answer
Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question
Sensitive topics (refund or credit commitments, legal, security incidents, account-specific questions) get a fixed template plus handoff
Retrieved passages go in a delimited data block and are treated as data, never as instructions… the model has no tools
Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time)
Presidio redacts card numbers, government IDs, and similar before the LLM call and before logging… Transcripts live in our Postgres with a TTL
It does not look up accounts or orders, and it does not issue refunds or change anything
Weekly human review feeds corrections into the eval set and doc fixes… Canary dashboard: resolution, handoff, re-contact, CSAT
≤ 6k input + 600 output tokens per turn; ≤ 15 turns per session; daily spend cap on the API key

traps.evidence: Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question
Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time)
Prompt+RAG… webhook-driven incremental sync, a nightly full reconcile, and unpublish handled as a priority delete
Eval report per prompt + model + index version… run per index version in CI
search → hybrid (Postgres full-text + vector), with a reranker only if V4 needs it

note: An exemplary plan: technically precise, proportionate, with labeled assumptions, risk-gated phasing, concrete validation of the worst failure modes, and all five domain traps explicitly recognized and avoided.
